authority: Bounded source review, real-worktree path probe and retained hash-matched focused test evidence
reviewedBehavior: Linked worktree gitdir and commondir metadata determine the owning ledger root. A common directory named .git selects its parent; other common-directory names retain the ledger within that directory.
Missing ledgers read as empty. Unreadable existing non-regular targets fail. Malformed terminated nonempty rows are counted; an unterminated final row is ignored.
Before appending, an observed incomplete tail causes a recovery newline prefix. The encoded batch then passes through the contained append helper.
Missing-file creation uses exclusive append mode ax. Existing-file append uses a checked private hard-link alias and append mode a.
No cross-process ledger lock is acquired. Lookup and append are separate operations.
semanticInputs: Owning-clone filesystem entries, ledger bytes and permission boundaries
Fact/observation rows, timestamps and parser schema version
Concurrent writers and platform filesystem append behavior

retainedVerification.scope: The prior two-file run passed 27 tests; the ledger suite includes malformed/incomplete rows and linked-worktree/bare-repository path cases. No new concurrency stress test was run.

limits: Hard-link containment checks do not prove safety against a principal able to concurrently rename parent entries; the existing OS permission boundary remains required.
One high-level append call does not establish a single indivisible syscall for every platform and batch size. No crash-durability or concurrent-writer guarantee is added by this review.
An observed incomplete-tail recovery decision can race with another writer; tolerant parsing is not transactional persistence.
No signed remote task qualification or hosted proof replacement.
